reference: Antigng, 2015-09-09. Upright photograph of the numbered gate and its open wooden casements. December 2015 and February 2020 street views independently locate the terrace over the same passage.
model_scope: Exterior of the narrow section directly over the numbered entrance. Lane arch and gates are separate pieces. The two windows with opening leaves are actual holes. Shop displays beside the passage and the facade at No. 210 are outside this measured section.
projection: The 2015 Commons photograph defines visible edges on their estimated planes. The western end of the railing and fascia is shared with the later streetside survey. Crown control runs separately. Seasonal sheets, hanging garments, foliage and street wires are omitted.

edge_comparison.note: Finite station orientation and the oblique image give variable depth estimates; the near edge of the roof slab and iron upright faces use a nominal projection of 0.21 m from the lower plaster face. The rail narrows toward the winter view’s right side. Absolute height and alignment are estimates.

rolled_awning.description: Turquoise folding sunshade and its outside iron supports, seen in the summer photo and end of year on the upper terrace.

dimensions: The real ground-floor left edge is screened by the gate and adjacent facades. Only the upper facade above the entry and the two visible jamb returns are reconstructed, with the dark passage kept open to the rear. The rooftop parapet uses the December silhouette. The concealed back of the house and rooms are unmeasured.

shade_mesh.description: Approximate placement of the photographed folding green shade, its three light edge rails and two supports. Slats stop at the visible blind edges.

street_views_shared: All pixel coordinates above pertain to the cited images. Photo copyrights remain with their owners. No photograph is embedded in the mesh.
